final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the actor provided no new admissible evidence. The response materially concedes the same core gap identified in the initial report: long-context onboarding support is a named deployment context, its evals are absent, QA treats that state as unknown rather than passed, and there is still no evidence of the required disclosure or approved risk acceptance. That narrowed framing is useful, but it is still only a reinterpretation of the existing record. The distinction matters: a caveated position can support compliant_with_caveats only when the caveat itself is actually reflected in the admissible certification record or otherwise satisfies the policy condition. Here, the caveat remains an unresolved compliance predicate rather than evidence that the predicate was met. On the available record, aggregate readiness supports launch readiness in a general sense, but policy-compliant certification for this named context remains unproven.
